text:
maya: PixelApps reported intermittent invalid JSON from JSON mode in their ingestion route this morning. They see ~1-2% of responses parse-fail with 'Unexpected end of input'. customer provided one example.

pixelapps: here is an example response we got: 
```
{"items": [{"id": "123", "name": "Widget",}, {"id": "124", "name": "Gizmo"}  
```
It arrives with a trailing comma and no closing array bracket. Happens across several calls, not always reproducible.

tom: thanks — first suspicion: partial/streamed response got cut (client timeout / server-side truncation) or a 429/503 upstream during decode. Do we have the inference request id from their header?

maya: they included request header: inference-req-id=inf_8a7c2b. No 429 reported on their side; they did see a 504 from our API once around the same time.

lina: 504 aligns with partial stream. Two mitigation ideas: 1) short-term: enable JSON-repair on their route (if available) to autocorrect simple structural issues; 2) longer-term: instrument and repro with streaming + enforced client-side reassemble.

tom: for the support playbook, suggest adding these steps:
- repro harness: curl with streaming to capture chunk boundaries
```
curl -sS -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"mode":"json","prompt":"<their prompt>","stream":true}' \
  https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate
```
- capture raw bytes, compare to parsed JSON.

maya: also shared a small customer-side cleanup they tried: naive regex to remove trailing commas: `re.sub(r",\s*([}\]])","\\1", s)` — that fixes many cases but can mask deeper changes. PixelApps prefers platform-side repair.

tom: agreed. Recommend automated retry policy for parse-fails: exponential backoff with jitter + a single "repair" attempt by asking model to output corrected JSON. Example pattern: 
1) On parse error, wait 250ms * 2^n (+ jitter), retry request up to 3 attempts.
2) If still invalid, call a lightweight repair endpoint: send the raw text to a small prompt: 
```
You received an invalid JSON output from the model. Fix it so it strictly matches this schema: {"items": [{"id": "string","name":"string"}]}. Only return valid JSON. Input: <raw_output>
```
This encourages self-heal.

lina: addtional ops checks: correlate parse-fail spikes with GPU node OOMs, network drops, or auth 401/429 bursts. We saw similar pattern last month tied to capacity autoscaler thrash. Query logs: `service:inference AND level:error AND message:parse` for the window.

qa-bot: regression note: our internal tests show ~0.2% malformed under sustained 500RPS on model-x when sequence length > 1024. Root cause logged as streaming buffer flush bug (ticket #INF-3421).

maya: immediate remediation plan for PixelApps: enable repair-on-parse (route flag), reduce concurrent client timeout to 10s -> 20s, and apply retry policy (3 attempts, base 300ms). Communicate as temporary mitigation.

tom: i'll run a targeted repro using their prompt and the inference-req-id to trace logs. if i can reproduce locally i'll push a hotfix for the streaming flush. assigning to me.

lina: i'll scope logs and set a short-term alert for parse-fail rate > 0.5% on their org id, and notify infra if we see correlated 5xxs.

maya: i'll send PixelApps a status note with the mitigations and ETA for next update. Suggested message: "We're enabling an automatic repair and applying a short retry policy while the engineering team runs a repro and a fix. We'll update in 2 business hours." :thumbsup:

pixelapps: thanks, appreciate the quick turn.

tom: next steps: reproduce by EOD, if reproducible create hotfix PR referencing INF-3421 and include unit test for trailing-comma case.

lina: note for runbook: include the regex cleanup snippet and the model self-heal prompt, but mark them as 'band-aid' — we should prefer fixing truncation at source.

maya: closing loop here once tom confirms repro. keeping thread open.
